requirement: For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, and every `{fixme}` reference except one inside a site under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.
rationale:
**Verdict: false.** Coverage checking works for `{impl}` and `{test}` references, but `{fixme}` references are never discovered or checked, and no `{fixme}` acknowledges that gap.

**Obligations**
1. Every `{impl}` reference in a source file, including one in a declaration, must be covered by an input of the referenced definition's evidence file. Same for `{test}`.
2. Every `{fixme}` reference must be covered the same way, except one inside a site under `site_review`.
3. A `{cite}` reference must not require coverage.
4. Every uncovered reference must be reported with its role, full name, file and line.

**Obligations 1, 3 and 4 are met.**
- `validate_references` (src/evidence.rs:1264-1456) builds the evidence path `evidence/<name>.json`. It resolves the recorded input ranges with `evidence_input_ranges` (src/evidence.rs:1612). It skips `ReferenceKind::Cite` and reports `no input covers {role}`name` at file:line` for each `{impl}` or `{test}` reference whose file and line fall outside every input range.
- `InputRange` (src/evidence.rs:1255) and `SourceRange` (src/inputs.rs:21) carry the ranges used for this check.
- Tests exist for these cases:
  - `source_references_are_covered_by_evidence_inputs` and `reports_unknown_references_and_uncovered_lines` cover covered and uncovered lines. The second asserts the role, name, file and line in the message.
  - `uncovered_cite_is_not_reported_while_uncovered_impl_and_test_are` covers cites being exempt, plus uncovered `{impl}` and `{test}` references being reported.
  - `cited_example_with_a_test_and_matching_evidence_validates` and tests/outcomes.rs `fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references` also exercise uncovered references.

**Obligation 2 is not met.**
- `ReferenceKind` (src/lib.rs:124-132) has only `Impl`, `Cite`, `Test` and `Term`.
- `reference_roles` (src/lib.rs:762-822) recognizes only `{impl}`, `{cite}`, `{test}` and `{term}`. A `{fixme}` reference is never parsed into a `SourceReference`.
- Because of that, `validate_references` never sees a `{fixme}` reference. An uncovered one would never be reported, and neither would the role, name, file and line.
- A ripgrep over `src` for `{fixme`, `"fixme"` and `Fixme` found no source-reference handling. The matches were only the FIXME determination handling, such as `Judgment::Fixme`.
- The "except inside a site under `site_review`" exclusion has no code either.
- No test checks that an uncovered `{fixme}` reference is reported or that a site `{fixme}` is exempt.

The gap is in `src/lib.rs` (`reference_roles`, `ReferenceKind`) and `validate_references`. No `{fixme}` reference acknowledges it, so it is an unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} evidence_coverage

For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, and every `{fixme}` reference except one inside a site under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.
:::{req} site_review
Every site of a distributed requirement under
{cite}`requirements.references.distributed` MUST have a site review: an
assessment of whether that site upholds the requirement, recorded at
`evidence/sites/<full-name>/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` and
`<selector>` are encoded as under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. The review MUST use the prompt
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.site_prompt`. Mandatory inputs, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the site's outline
node, the requirement's complete declaration, and each declaration the
requirement cites. The record MUST contain the requirement's full name, the
site's file and selector, `queries`, the sorted names of the queries with a
match at the site, `applies`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`, with
determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. `applies` MUST be a
Boolean recording whether the requirement applies to the site. A site to which
the requirement does not apply MUST be judged `true`, and the rationale MUST
explain why it does not apply. `habeas info` MUST report, for each selected
distributed requirement, how many of its sites the requirement does not apply
to.
Validation MUST require a current, accepted review for every site, MUST report a
false review with its rationale, and MUST report stale, missing, or orphaned
reviews; a review is orphaned when its file and selector no longer name a site
of the requirement. A `{fixme}` naming the requirement inside a site
acknowledges a gap at that site only: it MUST be an input to that site's review
and MUST NOT contribute to the requirement's own review, coverage, or reference
set. A review MUST become stale when the site's hash, the requirement's
declaration, a cited declaration, its `queries`, or the `{fixme}` references
naming the requirement inside the site, with the words of their bodies, change.
Each site review's determination MUST be checked on its own, independently of
the requirement's evidence. Authoring with `--all` MUST include site reviews,
`habeas author sites:<full-name>` MUST author the site reviews of the named
requirement, and `habeas author sites:<full-name>/<file>#<selector>` MUST author
the review of the one site it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>` names the
file's root node. `habeas status` MUST report missing, stale, invalid, and false
site reviews with their requirement, file, and selector, and `habeas info` MUST
list each selected requirement's sites with their determinations.
:::{req} reference_index
The harness MUST expose a `references` tool with this interface:
```text
references({ selection: String? }) -> ReferenceIndex
ReferenceIndex {
definitions: Array<DefinitionName>,
sites: Array<ReferenceSite>,
DefinitionName { name: String, kind: "requirement" | "example" }
ReferenceSite {
name: String,
role: "impl" | "cite" | "test",
file: String,
line: Integer?,
item: String?,
`selection` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`.
Without `selection`, the tool MUST return
the full name and kind of every requirement and named example in full-name
order, with empty `sites`. With `selection`, it MUST return the selected definitions
in full-name order and one flattened `sites` array containing every valid
`{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` reference to any match under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, each naming the definition it
references, ordered by name, file, and line. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST be reported as a site for its
anchored file without a line. A site in a supported language MUST give the
selector of its smallest enclosing outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`. Only sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` MUST contribute sites. If reading such a
source fails, the tool MUST return an explanatory tool error naming the source.
An invalid selection or one matching no definition MUST return an explanatory tool
error.
Results are listings without source text. Like directory listings, they MUST
NOT become evidence inputs; the model requests the sources it relies on with the
`habeas` tool.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
